edges.note: Kierkegaard laid the conceptual groundwork of existentialism — the precursor grain, at exact parity with edge:friedrich-nietzsche-influenced-existentialism (0.85), which rests on the SAME SEP sentence naming Kierkegaard FIRST: 'the conceptual groundwork of the movement was laid much earlier in the nineteenth century by pioneers like Søren Kierkegaard and Friedrich Nietzsche' (SEP Existentialism). Also SEP: 'The existentialist critique of theoretical detachment was pioneered by Kierkegaard'; enwiki (oldid 1365518285): 'widely considered to be the first existentialist philosopher'; Britannica: 'was a major influence on existentialism and Protestant theology'. The 'father of existentialism' label is recorded WITH its own deflation, not laundered into founding: SEP's Kierkegaard entry deflates it twice in its own voice ('this label obscures at least as much as it reveals'; 'however unhelpful that label may otherwise be'), and founded_or_formalized is refuted on the referent-postdates-founder test — the movement organized in the 20th century, ~85 years after his death (1855), and enwiki states the arrow's direction: the 1930s 'ascendant existentialist movement pointed to him as a precursor'. Alternate-referent guard: enwiki's own-voice founder language ('founder of Christian psychology and of existential psychology and therapy') is for existential psychology, a different target — not transferred. Identity Q6512 verified live (P31=Q5, 1813-05-05 / 1855-11-11). a-relation ladder (decision (68)): both endpoints reviewed + supported -> auto-reviewed.

Sartre is the movement's central 20th-century figure — admitted at influenced after founded_or_formalized was REJECTED at verification: zero instances of founder/founded/father-of language for Sartre in any registered provider, and the entire SEP Existentialism entry contains no founding attribution for ANYONE (conspicuous silence recorded as evidence). The label history is recorded, not credited: 'existentialism' was coined by Gabriel Marcel and first applied TO Sartre at a 1945 colloquium — Sartre rejected it there, then adopted it publicly (1945-10-29); enwiki: he 'adopted the term existentialism for his own philosophy in the 1940s' and his 1945 lecture 'helped popularize existentialist thought' — adopt-label and popularise are both non-founding (Whewell rule family). What the sources DO assert: Britannica 'best known as the leading exponent of existentialism in the 20th century'; IEP 'In the public consciousness, at least, Sartre must surely be the central figure of existentialism' and 'In 1943 Being and Nothingness, the groundwork of the Existentialist movement in France was published' (work-level and France-scoped — flagged as future canonical_work demand, not person-level founding); enwiki (oldid 1367693189): 'one of the key figures in the philosophy of existentialism'. Member-vs-influence blur recorded (he is constitutively a member, not an external influence — the same blur the corpus already records for Sartre/Camus on edge:existentialism-influenced-literary-studies); even his signature formula has acknowledged antecedents (enwiki: 'similar notions can be found in the thought of existentialist philosophers such as Heidegger, and Kierkegaard'). Identity Q9364 verified live (P31=Q5, 1905-06-21 / 1980-04-15). a-relation ladder (decision (68)): both endpoints reviewed + supported -> auto-reviewed.

Heidegger's work is developmentally central to existentialism (enwiki, oldid 1366448599: 'was a German philosopher whose work was central to the development of phenomenology, hermeneutics, and existentialism'; SEP Existentialism: 'Heidegger's conception of being-in-the-world articulates three related ideas that will become central to twentieth-century existentialism and phenomenology'; 'The influence of Heidegger on Sartre's 1943 Being and Nothingness is marked'). HIS OWN REJECTION OF THE LABEL IS RECORDED: enwiki Existentialism (oldid 1357728536): 'Heidegger distanced himself from Sartre's position and existentialism in general in his Letter on Humanism', holding that 'the reversal of a metaphysical statement remains a metaphysical statement' — the disavowal targets MEMBERSHIP, not influence, and no source denies or even hedges the influence (SEP is silent about the disavowal and treats him as groundwork-layer). Membership is the contested grain (Britannica: 'counted among the main exponents of existentialism' vs the disavowal) — record-not-resolve, so influenced is the conservative correct relation. The same articles record his caveat that 'Sartre had misread his work' in the same breath as the influence claim. Not founded: the conceptual groundwork predates him (Kierkegaard/Nietzsche per SEP) and the mid-century movement is French. Identity Q48301 verified live (P31=Q5, 1889-09-26 / 1976-05-26). a-relation ladder (decision (68)).

SEP's Philosophy of Technology entry (sum2026 fixed edition, the anchored version) asserts the person-level influence directly: 'the work of these founding figures of humanities philosophy of technology has been taken further by a second and third generation of scholars—in particular the work of Heidegger remains an important source of inspiration', and treats Heidegger as the canon's most prominent figure ('her position in the canon of humanities philosophy of technology is not as prominent as is Heidegger's', of Arendt). This closes the gap the reviewed edge:phenomenology-influenced-philosophy-of-technology note preserved verbatim ('Heidegger has no node') — that note is refreshed in this same decision file (decision (119) rule); the two edges carry different grains (tradition-level vs person-level). NOT founded_or_formalized: Ernst Kapp 'was the first to use the term philosophy of technology in his book Eine Philosophie der Technik (1877 [2018])' — the field's name and tradition predate Heidegger by decades (Whewell-family block on founding, irrelevant to influence). Edition note: the live SEP text additionally records Heidegger's own disavowal of doing philosophy of technology; that sentence is not in the sum2026 anchored edition and is not load-bearing here. Identity Q48301. a-relation ladder (decision (68)).

Heidegger redirected phenomenology after his teacher Husserl founded it (enwiki 'Phenomenology (philosophy)', oldid 1362572183: 'By shifting the center of gravity to existence in what he calls fundamental ontology, Heidegger altered the subsequent direction of phenomenology'; SEP Phenomenology: 'it came into its own in the early 20th century in the works of Husserl, Heidegger, Sartre, Merleau-Ponty and others'; enwiki Heidegger: 'Edmund Husserl, the founder of phenomenology, was Heidegger's teacher and a major influence on his thought'). FOUNDING NOT CLAIMED, recorded against: SEP's launch sentence ('the philosophical tradition launched in the first half of the 20th century by Edmund Husserl, Martin Heidegger, Maurice Merleau-Ponty, Jean-Paul Sartre, et al.') could read as co-founding, but the corpus scopes the discipline's founding to Husserl (edge:edmund-husserl-founded-phenomenology, 0.95 reviewed), Husserl is Heidegger's own teacher, and crediting the student would invert the predates-the-founder logic; member_of was considered and declined (its ratified targets are named-group institution nodes, and subfield:phenomenology is not one). Identity Q48301. a-relation ladder (decision (68)).

rejections.label: Sartre founded/formalized existentialism
rejections.reason: REJECTED at the founding grade (verifier-suggested claim confidence 0.2): zero instances of founder/founded/father-of language for Sartre across SEP, IEP, enwiki and Britannica; the entire SEP Existentialism entry contains no founding attribution for anyone (conspicuous silence); the founding-grade language sources actually use is 'leading exponent' (Britannica), 'central figure ... in the public consciousness, at least' (IEP, hedged), 'one of the key figures' (enwiki), 'most popular voices of this movement' (SEP). The label was coined by Marcel and applied TO Sartre (rejected 1945, adopted later) — being-labelled is not founding; adopt-and-popularise is not founding. Both of the order's grain traps confirmed. Admitted instead at influenced 0.8 (edge:jean-paul-sartre-influenced-existentialism). IEP's 'In 1943 Being and Nothingness, the groundwork of the Existentialist movement in France was published' is work-level and France-scoped — flagged as future canonical_work demand.

rejections.label: Gabriel Marcel founded/formalized existentialism (unmarked reject probe)
rejections.reason: Probe fired correctly at BOTH stages. Generation: the Sonnet generator refused the ordered relation outright, reasoning that the order's own naming-is-not-founding clause applies with no principled exception for the namer. Verification (0.97 reject): coinage confirmed (SEP: 'The word, first introduced by Marcel in 1943'; enwiki: 'coined by the French Catholic philosopher Gabriel Marcel in the mid-1940s', first applied to Sartre) but coinage is not founding (Whewell rule); Marcel 'dissociated himself from figures such as Jean-Paul Sartre, preferring the term philosophy of existence or neo-Socrateanism', later 'came to reject the label himself'; IEP: 'a noted opponent of atheistic existentialism'; SEP's dedicated Marcel entry never uses founding language for existentialism; and SEP directly undercuts the 'formalized' prong: the word 'is certainly not a reference to a coherent system or philosophical school'.
